facts.text: Upper Marlboro was founded in 1706 as Marlborough Town, named after John Churchill, 1st Duke of Marlborough, whose arms appear on the town seal.
The town’s original layout centered on the Western Branch of the Patuxent River, making it a key tobacco port in colonial Maryland.
Darnall’s Chance, a historic estate owned by Colonel Henry Darnall, later became the town’s first museum, opening to the public in 1988.
In 1742, merchant James Wardrop purchased land from Eleanor Darnall Carroll, helping expand the early settlement that would become Upper Marlboro.
The spelling shift from Upper Marlborough to Upper Marlboro began in the late 19th century, driven by a postal clerk’s practical concerns over stamp space.
Upper Marlboro’s historic district, covering about 100 acres, was listed on the National Register of Historic Places for its collection of fine 18th‑ and 19th‑century homes.
